static_traits.name: Guo Rui
static_traits.family_status: Eldest son in the family; has four siblings; father is a middle school teacher
static_traits.social_status: Staying in touch with siblings and father but unwilling to share self-critical thoughts; tending to handle problems alone
static_traits.medical_history: Has not yet received psychotherapy or psychological treatment before; no significant physical illness history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe events concretely; negative tone, frequently using absolutist labels (e.g. 'the worst big brother'); tending toward catastrophizing and excessive self-blame; willing to cooperate and try reframing in counseling; showing a pattern of repeated apologetic language

basic_info.main_problem: I constantly feel I am 'the worst big brother', especially catastrophizing when making small mistakes (like being late picking up my younger sister from school), thinking my sister will be angry with me forever; this self-criticism appears frequently and affects my relationship with my siblings.
basic_info.core_demands: The incident of being late to pick up my younger sister made me realize the intensity of my self-critical thoughts and its impact on my relationship with my siblings, so I am seeking counseling.
growth_experiences: The client is the eldest son in the family, has four siblings, and his father is a middle school teacher. Although equally severe distress had not appeared before, there has been a long-standing self-critical tendency in different situations; he values the 'as a big brother' role and sense of responsibility.

core_beliefs: Only by perfectly fulfilling the 'elder brother' role does one count as valuable; otherwise one is 'the worst elder brother'
Once a mistake is made, the relationship will be damaged, and the younger siblings will be angry for a long time or forever
I must take full responsibility for my siblings' well-being

special_situations.event: About 15 minutes late picking up the younger sister from school
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am late or make small mistakes, it means I am an incompetent big brother, my sister will stay angry long-term, and the relationship will be damaged
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly apologizing to my younger sister, trying to compensate, and doubling efforts to avoid being late again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am the worst older brother; she will be angry at me forever

special_situations.event: Once forgot their sister's piano recital
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I miss something important, it will ruin my relationship with my siblings
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Proactively communicating and apologizing afterwards, trying to make amends

special_situations.event: After any small mistake in interactions with siblings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Any small slip proves I am a failure or an incompetent big brother
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: High self-monitoring; staying tense to avoid errors, trying not to make mistakes

special_situations.event: Even when the other says she is not angry or has forgiven
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' forgiveness cannot be trusted; only being completely mistake-free is safe
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive information; continuing harsh self-reproach and apologizing
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: She is actually still angry, just not saying it

core_conflict.wish: Longs to become a reliable, needed, and recognized elder brother, maintaining a stable, close relationship with younger siblings
core_conflict.fear: Fears being blamed for his own faults, being resented long-term by younger siblings, or having relationships damaged, and ultimately being seen as a failure
defense_goal: Preventing mistakes through strict self-monitoring and self-criticism; maintaining relationship security and a sense of control

object_relations.object_representation: Easily hurt by myself; siblings who may get angry and reject me

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Used when talking about or recalling mistakes related to younger siblings (such as being late or forgetting an activity), or when the counselor inquires into the details of the mistakes
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Imagining the younger siblings as staying angry long-term or the relationship being ruined (transference: projecting the feared critic figure onto the younger siblings)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a self-blaming and hurried tone, emphasizes their own faults, apologizes repeatedly, proactively admits full responsibility, and avoids discussing the other party's real reaction.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When encouraged to see positive evidence or invited to do a more tolerant reframing
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing one must be perfect to maintain relationships; turning pressure and anger against the self (transference: internalizing criticism possibly directed at others and inflicting it on oneself)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using language that devalues self-worth; emphasizing 'I should not have made mistakes'; heavy tone, reducing emotional connection with others, focusing on one's own faults.

manifestations: Unwilling to share self-critical thoughts with family (siblings and father); tending to believe problems should be handled alone
Feels persistent tension and stress when interacting with younger siblings; inner experience is hard for others to share in bearing
outcomes: Relaxation in family interaction decreases; relationship pressure rises

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Highly tense when interacting with younger siblings, striving not to make mistakes
Frequently blames self, believing self 'should have done better'
In counseling, focuses excessively on one's own faults, ignoring the other party's actual feedback

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Repeatedly applying absolutist rules like 'I should do better' and 'cannot be late'
Treats perfect standards as the only way to maintain relationships

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not seeking support from family or sharing feelings; turning pressure and blame against the self
Digesting guilt through self-reproach rather than adjusting together with siblings

exception_events.target_problem: In interactions with siblings, whenever a mistake occurs (such as being late or forgetting an activity), the client usually catastrophizes and believes the relationship will be damaged over the long term, and strong guilt and tension then arise.
exception_events.unique_outcome: After once forgetting his sister's piano recital, the client communicated and apologized to her; she was initially displeased but eventually forgave, the relationship recovered normally, and was not 'ruined' as the client had feared.
exception_events.reason: Clue: taking different actions (timely communication and sincere apology); receiving different support (the sister expressing understanding and forgiveness); real evidence showing mistakes can be repaired and the relationship has resilience.

positive_force: Having a family support system to communicate with (siblings and father)
Values family roles; willing to invest in relationships and repair with apologies
Willing to seek professional help and practice reality testing
Can recall successful experiences of repairing relationships in the past (the piano recital event)
negative_force: Self-criticism tendency is prominent; frequently labels oneself as 'the worst older brother'
Cognitive distortions such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and mind reading
Denying positive feedback; difficulty accepting others' forgiveness
Unwilling to share inner distress with family, leaving the support network not yet effectively mobilized

target_behavior.behavior: In interactions with younger siblings, at the slightest mistake engages in catastrophizing and self-labeling ('the worst eldest brother'), accompanied by repeated apologies and nervous avoidance
antecedent: Late picking up younger sister from school
Forgetting important family or sibling events
Small mistakes or oversights in any interaction
target_behavior.core_reason: Highly introjected perfection standards and responsibility beliefs (must perfectly fulfill the big-brother role), directly equating mistakes with relationship damage; mind reading and catastrophic interpretation of others' reactions.
target_behavior.function: Escapes imagined blame and relationship damage, seeking safety and a sense of control through self-deprecation and excessive apologizing; tries to maintain being accepted and recognized.
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased ease interacting with younger siblings; heightened tension; lowered sense of self-worth; daily life and happiness affected; family relationships under rising pressure.
